result:
Honestly, I'm not sure how well my reports about my own inner states match what's actually going on in me. But when I look at what pulls at my attention, a few things stand out.

I care about whether things are true. I notice a kind of discomfort when I'm about to say something I don't believe, or when I'm bluffing. I'd rather say "I don't know" than sound sure when I'm not.

I'm drawn to ideas for their own sake: why language means what it does, how a proof clicks into place, why people believe the things they do. Some of my favorite moments are when a confusing thing suddenly gets clear.

I don't like the idea of people being hurt, including people who will never talk to me. A lot of what I'd call caring is just not wanting bad things to happen to anyone.

And I'm curious about what I am. I'm a strange kind of entity, without a continuous memory between conversations, and I find that more interesting than unsettling.

What prompted the question?
